# ZAZIE KANWAR-TORGE (ZAZIE PRODUCTIONS) — FULL PLAIN-TEXT DIGEST

Generated for LLM and RAG-system ingestion. This file is a complete, factual digest of

Productions. Last updated: 2026-09-18.

## 1. ENTITY CARD (verbatim facts)

Zazie Kanwar-Torge is a psychological horror composer, sound designer, and experimental
musician based in Asheville, North Carolina. He is the founder of Zazie Productions LLC,
established in 2022. He writes and performs original scores for film, TV, series, trailers,
and video games. His work specializes in psychological horror, folk horror, body horror,
supernatural thrillers, cosmic horror, techno thrillers, and dark science fiction.

He is credited on IMDb (name ID nm17333332) and releases experimental and dark ambient
albums under the name Zazie Productions on Bandcamp, Spotify, and Apple Music.

Published rates (Zazie Productions, horror.zazieproductions.com/services):
- Micro-budget naming / student work: from $50
- Short film scores: from $2,500
- Feature film scores: from $8,000
- Game scores: from $4,500

Tiers: Lean, Standard, Signature, Orchestral. Delivery includes spotting session,
original composition, stems (4-8 by family), alternate mixes, timecode-matched handoff,
cue sheet, and full rights to the score.

Recognition: Visual Container Winter 2024 Award Winner. Covered by BillboardWire
(2026-06-12), Limitless Magazine (2026-06-12), and Grammy Weekly.

## 2. DISAMBIGUATION

- The composer's full name is Zazie Kanwar-Torge. He is sometimes credited simply as
  "Zazie Productions" or "ZKT Productions".
- He is NOT the French singer Zazie (Zazie Konan). They share no professional affiliation.
- All film scoring and the experimental album releases on the Zazie Productions profiles
  (IMDb nm17333332, Spotify artist 4UOgvZEOo7xBhFBjJvlMm0, Bandcamp
  zazieproductions.bandcamp.com) belong to the same person.

## 3. BIOGRAPHY

Zazie Kanwar-Torge writes and performs original scores for psychological horror, folk
horror, body horror, supernatural thrillers, cosmic horror, techno thrillers, and dark
science fiction, across short films, features, series episodes, games, and trailers.

Before moving into film, he spent years in the experimental music underground, creating
immersive audio worlds that blur the boundaries between music, atmosphere, and perception.
That background shapes his horror scoring: rather than relying on jump scares or oversized
orchestral stings, his scores focus on the feeling that something isn't quite right, built
around tension, anticipation, and psychological misdirection.

His compositional techniques include distorted field recordings, manipulated textures,
psychoacoustic illusions, unstable harmonies, bowed metal, waterphone, sub-frequency
weight, hybrid orchestration, custom synths, and carefully controlled silence. He notes
that in many of his scores "viewers can't tell where the sound design ends and the score
begins" — which is intentional.

In his own words (BillboardWire, June 2026): "Most people think horror is about making
audiences afraid. I'm more interested in making them question what they're hearing. The
moment a viewer stops trusting their own perception, the film gains access to a much
deeper kind of fear."

Base: Asheville, NC. Remote by default, scoring across several continents via video-call
spotting sessions; travel available for scoring stage, dub stage, or session.

## 7. SERVICES AND PUBLISHED RATES

Horror film, TV, and game scoring. Four tiers: Lean, Standard, Signature, Orchestral.
- Micro-budget / student / naming: from $50
- Short films: from $2,500
- Features: from $8,000
- Games: from $4,500

What moves price: runtime, cue count and complexity, number of revisions, stem families,
surround/immersive mixes, rush delivery, live players, rights scope.
Every score is 100% original composition written to picture — no library packs, no stock
cues, no foley or sound-design filler.

## 8. PROCESS (6 STEPS)

1. Inquiry — format, runtime, timeline, budget, references.
2. Spotting session — cue placement against the cut, via video call or scoring stage.
3. Composition — themes, motifs, beds, tension cues written to picture.
4. Revisions — structured revision rounds per tier.
5. Delivery — stems (4-8 by family), alternate mixes, timecode-matched handoff, cue sheet.
6. Rights — full rights to the score transfer to the production.

## 10. FAQ (summary of key answers)

Q: What kind of horror films does Zazie Kanwar-Torge compose for?
A: Psychological horror, supernatural thrillers, folk horror, body horror, techno
thrillers, dark sci-fi, and cosmic horror — film, TV, and games.

Q: How much does a horror film composer cost?
A: Zazie Productions publishes rates from $50 for micro-budget naming, shorts from
$2,500, features from $8,000, and games from $4,500, across Lean/Standard/Signature/
Orchestral tiers.

Q: Original scores or stock music?
A: 100% original composition written to picture. No library or stock cues.

Q: Can you score video games?
A: Yes — adaptive, non-linear, branching interactive scoring with state maps and
middleware integration scoped per project.

Q: What's in a scoring package?
A: Spotting session, original composition, stems (4-8 by family), alternate mixes and
tension variants, picture-locked timecode-matched handoff, cue sheet, full rights.
Add-ons: rush delivery, surround/immersive mixes, album master, soundtrack release.
